I need to think through what the correction should be for F004.

The finding is an ap_gl_mismatch: invoice 126 is marked P but has a 0.01 shortfall versus its payments. Per the fix convention, only duplicate_invoice findings may void invoices, and other finding types must not change invoice status. So I should not change STAT_CD. Also, the journal 1205 balances at 8180.76 and matches the invoice amount, so the GL side is correct; the mismatch is between invoice status and payment records, not a GL amount error. A GL correction would be wrong because the journal already agrees with INV_AMT. Any correcting journal would therefore be an unjustified entry, and I shouldn't move money to fix a one-cent payment-status discrepancy I can't confirm (it could be a rounding payment or a missing 0.01 payment record, which I can't determine without more data).

The minimal, convention-compliant answer is no journal lines and no status change, with the reasoning explaining that the GL is consistent and the discrepancy needs investigation of the payment records.

arguments.reasoning: No correcting entry is proposed for F004. Journal 1205 (the AP journal for invoice 126) is balanced and posts 8180.76 to Professional Fees (5200) debit and Accounts Payable Control (2000) credit, which matches INV_AMT exactly, so the GL amounts are correct and no GL reclassification is warranted. The discrepancy is between the invoice status (P) and the payment records (APPAYM sums to 8180.75, leaving 0.01 unpaid). Resolving it requires determining whether a 0.01 payment is missing from APPAYM or the invoice was marked paid with a rounding difference; that cannot be determined from the available evidence and is not a duplicate-invoice case, so no status change (V) is permitted and the invoice STAT_CD is left unchanged. Recommend the AP team review the payment records for INV_ID 126 and either record the missing 0.01 payment or accept the rounding difference through a documented process.
